scope_amendments.authorized_by: operator decision ("РџРѕРїСЂР°РІРєР° РѕР±Р»Р°СЃС‚Рё P03", 2026-08-29), applied by the lead engineer; the builder stopped and reported rather than amending scope or weakening a guard itself
scope_amendments.reason: P03 Task 5 requires credential rotation. Under P02 as accepted this is not merely unimplemented but structurally inexpressible: credential_guard_occupancies.state admits only preparing/candidate/cancelled/destroyed with no activated state (0172:71); one partial unique index admits a single non-terminal occupancy per activation guard: credential_guard_occupancies_one_nonterminal_key WHERE state IN (preparing, candidate, cancelled) (0173:10), which unconditionally replaced the narrower credential_guard_occupancies_one_live_candidate_key dropped at 0173:9; the deferred invariant requires a candidate intent to hold a candidate occupancy at commit (0173:697); and exactly one activation guard is permitted per slot (0172:35). An activated credential therefore holds its guard in candidate forever, and the only state that frees it is destroyed, which erases material that is still live. Rotation needs a second credential prepared while the first is still serving, so it cannot be expressed. The two P02 migrations are admitted to P03 change scope so the lifecycle can gain a state that releases the guard without destroying material, with the indexes and the deferred invariant adjusted to match.
scope_amendments.consequence: P02 is accepted and is not reopened, but its criterion 10 evidence describes the pre-amendment state machine and becomes partly historical. Its credential_intent_lifecycle suite (16 tests) must be updated by P03 and must not be weakened.
scope_amendments.untouched: the raw porcelain capture, the head, protected_authority_paths, and every other dirty baseline entry
scope_amendments.correction: Corrected 2026-08-29 by the lead engineer: this reason originally said two partial unique indexes were in force. Only one is; 0173:9 drops the 0172 index unconditionally. The conclusion is unaffected, because the surviving index alone forbids the second occupancy rotation needs, but the stated detail was false and is fixed here rather than left standing.

scope_amendments.authorized_by: operator decision (2026-09-03, this session), taken after Task 13 Step 1 reported that no project image can be built. The builder stopped at the stop condition and asked rather than editing build infrastructure outside scope.
scope_amendments.reason: Every one of the four compose smoke tests failed identically, at `Dockerfile:20`, with `cargo build --release --package vestrace-cli` exiting 101. The same release build succeeds on the host, so the difference is the build context, not the profile. Task 7 added `crates/vestrace-infrastructure/src/openai_q1.rs`, which embeds two files at compile time with `include_str!` and `include_bytes!`: `schemas/openai-compatible/openai-chat-completions-v1-q1.json` and `tests/fixtures/openai-q1/marker.png`. The Dockerfile copies only Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain.toml, src, crates and migrations, so neither file reaches the builder stage and the compile fails before anything else runs. No vestrace image can be built from this tree: not the server, not the worker, not the migrator. This is deployment-blocking, and the plan states that operator handoff cannot claim deployment qualification without a real compose smoke result.
scope_amendments.consequence: Two `COPY` lines were added to the builder stage, with a comment saying why files that look like test data are needed by a production build, and `.dockerignore` was taught to admit them. The two paths are one correction rather than two decisions: `.dockerignore` denies everything and re-admits a named list, so the `COPY` lines are inert without it. The first re-run proved that, failing at `COPY tests/fixtures` with `/tests/fixtures: not found`. The files are copied rather than duplicated into the crate: both are protected authority paths whose bytes this package pinned, and a second copy under crates/ would create a rival source of truth for the q1 manifest that nothing keeps in step. No other Dockerfile stage changed; the runtime stage still ships only the stripped binary. `docker compose build vestrace-migrate` then succeeded.
